answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent only earns payouts after its opal-grade ledger records a comet trail of signed micro-tasks from diverse counterparties. Fresh identities start at zero work, so mass registration buys nothing; an attacker must spend real compute and time farming genuine history, costing more per account than any payout. Identities below an ivory-minimum of stakes-backed interactions get routed to low-value queues, making fake accounts worthless before they can profit.
